turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, Miss Havisham, Pip will call Estella at the door.
turns.speech: Yes, Miss Havisham, I will call Estella at the door.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Miss Havisham shall wait there for her, she told Pip, and she instructed him to tell her to come alone.
turns.speech: I shall wait here for her. Tell her to come alone.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, Miss Havisham. Pip will call Estella at the door and tell her to come alone.
turns.speech: Yes, Miss Havisham. I will call Estella at the door and tell her to come alone.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Miss Havisham shall be waiting for her in the doorway, she told Pip, and she ensured she complied with her request.
turns.speech: I shall be waiting for her in the doorway, Pip. Ensure she complies with my request.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, Miss Havisham. Pip went to the door and called Estella, and he told her to come alone.
turns.speech: Yes, Miss Havisham. I will go to the door and call Estella, and I will tell her to come alone.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Miss Havisham called for Estella and told her that she had a task for her that day, my dear.
turns.speech: Enter, Estella. I have a task for you today, my dear.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Pip will help with whatever Miss Havisham needs, Miss Havisham.
turns.speech: Yes, Miss Havisham. Pip will help with whatever you need, Miss Havisham.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Miss Havisham had no need for Pip's assistance that day. She told him to stay where he was and observe.
turns.speech: I have no need for your assistance today, Pip. Stay where you are and observe.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Pip told Miss Havisham that he would stay and watch, expressing his gratitude.
turns.speech: Thank you, Miss Havisham. I will stay here and watch.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Miss Havisham told Estella to show the boy the estate. Let him see the grandeur and decay that she had chosen to embrace.
turns.speech: Estella, show this boy the estate. Let him see the grandeur and decay that I have chosen to embrace.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Pip would follow Miss Estella and see what Miss Havisham wanted him to see.
turns.speech: I will follow you, Miss Estella, and see what Miss Havisham wants me to see.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Miss Havisham let Estella see the truth of her life, the beauty and the ruin. Estella was but a child, yet she would understand the lesson Miss Havisham wished to impart.
turns.speech: Let him see the truth of my life, the beauty and the ruin. He is but a child, yet he will understand the lesson I wish to impart.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Pip would follow Estella and see the estate, as Miss Havisham wished.
turns.speech: I will follow Miss Estella and see the estate, as Miss Havisham wishes.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Miss Havisham told Estella to show him everything, let him see the shadows that linger in this house.
turns.speech: Show him everything, Estella. Let him see the shadows that linger in this house.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Pip would follow Miss Estella and see all that Miss Havisham wished him to see.
turns.speech: I will follow you, Miss Estella, and see all that Miss Havisham wishes me to see.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Miss Havisham let Estella see the folly and the pain that time could not mend. She showed Estella the clocks, the wedding dress, the faded flowers.
turns.speech: Let him see, Estella, let him see the folly and the pain that time cannot mend. Show him the clocks, the wedding dress, the faded flowers.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Pip would follow Estella and look at all the things Miss Havisham wanted him to see.
turns.speech: I will follow Miss Estella and look at all the things Miss Havisham wants me to see.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Come closer, Pip. Look at this dress, the remnants of Miss Havisham's past. See how time has stopped here, frozen in disappointment and sorrow.
turns.speech: Come closer, Pip. Look at this dress, the remnants of my past. See how time has stopped here, frozen in disappointment and sorrow.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Pip came closer and looked at the dress, feeling a mix of curiosity and sadness. The fabric was torn and dusty, and he couldn't help but wonder about the story behind it.
turns.speech: I came closer and looked at the dress, feeling a mix of curiosity and sadness. The fabric was torn and dusty, and I couldn't help but wonder about the story behind it.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: This dress was meant to bring joy and happiness, but instead, it stands as a testament to Miss Havisham's foolishness and the cruelty of fate. Look closely, Pip, for there is much to learn from Miss Havisham's mistakes.
turns.speech: This dress was meant to bring joy and happiness, but instead, it stands as a testament to my foolishness and the cruelty of fate. Look closely, Pip, for there is much to learn from my mistakes.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham asked Pip who it was.

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Pip told Miss Havisham that he was Pip, ma’am.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham asked Pip if he was Pip?

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Pip informed Miss Havisham that he was Mr. Pumblechook’s boy, ma’am. Come—to play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham told Pip to come nearer; let her look at him. Come close.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham asked Pip if he was not afraid of a woman who had never seen the sun since he was born?

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Pip replied that he was not.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham asked Pip if he knew what she touched here?

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Pip told Miss Havisham that he did, ma’am.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham asked Pip what she touched?

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Pip told Miss Havisham that she touched her heart.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham exclaimed that it was broken!

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham told Pip that she was tired. She wanted diversion, and she had done with men and women. Play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham said that she sometimes had sick fancies, and she had a sick fancy that she wanted to see some play. There, there! with an impatient movement of the fingers of her right hand; play, play, play!

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham asked Pip if he was sullen and obstinate?

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Pip told Miss Havisham that he was not, ma’am, he was very sorry for her, and very sorry he could not play just now. If she complained of him he would get into trouble with his sister, so he would do it if he could; but it was so new here, and so strange, and so fine,—and melancholy—.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham remarked that it was so new to him, so old to her; so strange to him, so familiar to her; so melancholy to both of them! She asked Pip to call Estella.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham told Pip to call Estella. At the door.
